differs significantly between Serous and endometrioid samples. | signedlogp.rna: The signedlogp.rna column is the −log10 (p-value) of the RNA‐level differential expression between serous and Gene: The Gene column specifies the gene in which each detected peptide variant occurs. | Variant: The “Variant” column lists the specific mutation observed in the peptide (e.g. the amino-acid substitution or allele change) as detected by the proteomic/genomic analysis. | Q-value: The Q-value is the false discovery rate (FDR)–adjusted p-value, i.e. the minimum FDR at which that peptide–variant identification would be called significant. | P-value: The P-value here is the statistical significance of each variant peptide’s spectrum match—i.e. the probability that the observed match arose by chance. | Peptide: The amino-acid sequence of the detected peptide (i.e., the variant-containing peptide identified in the experiment). | MassDiff: MassDiff: the difference (e.g. in daltons) between the observed peptide mass in the MS data and its theoretical/reference mass, reflecting the mass shift introduced by the variant. | Known_SNP: Indicates the dbSNP identifier (rs-number) or flag showing that the peptide’s amino acid change matches a previously reported single‐nucleotide polymorphism. | Chromosome: The Chromosome column denotes which chromosome (e.g. 1–22, X, Y, M) harbors the genomic variant linked to the observed peptide. | Hyperscore: Hyperscore: the MS/MS search‐engine confidence score (e.g. from X!Tandem) that quantifies the quality of the peptide–spectrum match. | Expectation: The “Expectation” column is the E-value from the peptide‐spectrum matching algorithm – i.e. the expected number of random matches scoring as well as (or better than) the observed one, used to gauge identification confidence. | Variant_Type: The Variant_Type column classifies the underlying genetic alteration for each peptide (e.g. missense, nonsense, frameshift, insertion, deletion). | Samples_With_Peptide: The Samples_With_Peptide column is a (typically comma-separated) list of the sample identifiers in which that peptide variant was detected. | Num_Samples_With_Peptide: The `Num_Samples_With_Peptide` column gives the count of individual samples in which that peptide was detected.

Alt: The “Alt” column lists the alternative (mutant) nucleotide(s) observed at the variant position. | Ref: The “Ref” column gives the reference (wild-type) nucleotide at the variant position. | End: The “End” column specifies the genomic end coordinate (the last base position) of the variant on the given chromosome. | Chr: The “Chr” column indicates the chromosome (e.g., 1, 2, X) on which the genomic variant underlying the predicted neoantigen is located. | mRNA: The mRNA column gives the specific transcript (mRNA) identifier or cDNA‐level change annotation (e.g. a RefSeq or Ensembl transcript accession with its nucleotide variant) in which the neoantigen-causing mutation occurs. | Gene: The “Gene” column lists the official symbol of the gene in which the somatic variant occurs and from which the predicted neoantigen peptide is derived. | Start: The “Start” column gives the genomic start coordinate (on the reference chromosome) at which the variant begins. | sample: The “sample” column gives the identifier of the biological sample (e.g. patient or tumor specimen) in which the neoantigen‐bearing variant was detected. | HLA_type: The HLA_type column specifies the particular HLA class I allele (e.g. HLA-A*02:01) against which the neoepitope’s binding affinity was predicted. | AA_after: The `AA_after` column gives the amino acid residue(s) present after the
